newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees 1997 GNP growth at 7-8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees 1997 GNP growth at 7-8 pct.

text.p: The Philippines said on Friday it expected gross national product (GNP) to grow by seven to eight percent in 1997 against the estimated 6.5 to 7.5 percent this year.

"With the short term stabilisation measures on track and most structural adjustment measures firmed up, GNP growth is targeted to reach 7.0 to 8.0 percent in real terms in 1997," Socio Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito told reporters at a year-end briefing.
Gross domestic product (GDP) was seen growing in 1997 by 7.1 to 7.8 percent against the expected 6.0 percent in 1996, he said.
Gross international reserves (GIR) could reach close to $14 billion in 1997, Habito said. As of mid-August this year, the country's GIR had reached a record high of $11.314 billion.
Habito said the government expected average inflation at about 6.5 percent in 1997. This year, the average inflation rate is expected to be at 8.7 percent.
The 6.5 percent inflation target would take the Philippines closer to the ASEAN norm of 4.0 to 5.0 percent, Habito said.
The Philippines is a part of ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) whose other members are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
